title: Staff Engineer - Platform & Tooling
descriptionHtml:
Who is Atominvest

Atominvest is the operating system for modern private markets asset managers. Our modular, flexible SaaS technology underpins key investor- and portfolio-management workflows.

Our customers are sophisticated private equity, growth equity, and private credit firms managing billions in assets globally. We aim to deliver ongoing high-quality outcomes for them through a long-term partnership mindset.

At Atominvest, you’ll be working on something very exciting: the future of work, investments and sustainability/ ethical investing for the world’s best investors and delivering a positive impact through this. Based on the growth we are experiencing, we think we’re on to something big.

It won’t be easy. Joining a scale up business is an amazing and rewarding challenge, pushing well beyond the boundaries of natural growth cycles. You’ll move quicker than feels comfortable and be brilliant at continually re-prioritizing what must get done to keep Atominvest growing year over year at the pace of the best SaaS companies on the planet.

We’ve gone from zero to ten, now we’re looking to go from ten to one hundred!

About the role

Hi, I'm Thomas, VP Engineering at Atominvest. This is the hire I'm most excited about, so I wanted to tell you about it myself.

You'll own the platform our clients run on and build the AI development harness our engineers work in day to day. That work runs from infrastructure to application code, so we're looking for an experienced engineer with breadth across both, and depth in at least one. Together, it's what lets a small, lean team, working alongside AI agents, ship like a much bigger one.

 

By platform, we mean everything our product and our engineers stand on: infrastructure, security, test automation, developer experience, and the agent pipelines that run through all of them. It's a broad, hands-on role. You'll write infrastructure as code for a new service one day and address network vulnerabilities the next, then enhance our AI development harness and release a new feature, all within the same month.

 

You might be a platform engineer who loves shipping product, or a full-stack engineer who has run serious production infrastructure. Either works.

As deployments grow more complex, the team needs your depth in infrastructure and distributed systems. You'll strengthen the architecture and make the design decisions the platform will rest on for years. Those decisions should leave room to grow, because future products may bring much larger volumes of data than we handle today.

It has to stay dependable while we do it. Our software needs to be available around the clock, every day of the year, and data integrity is critical. Our clients use Atominvest to report to their own investors, so a wrong number matters as much as an outage. Security, reliability and audit-readiness matter too. If you enjoy getting those right without slowing everything else down, you'll find plenty of fun things to work on.

The machine that builds the product

We're becoming AI-native. Agents do more and more of the mechanical work of writing code, and engineers build the machine that builds the product: the architecture, the specs, the limits agents work within, and the evals that tell us whether their output is right.

I think that moves an engineer's leverage upstream. When code is cheap, the scarce things are judgement and understanding. Which problem is worth solving? What does good look like for the person using it? Is the output actually right? Did what we shipped help? The best engineers I've worked with always solved the end problem, with code as the medium. Now that's most of the job.

That's why product and user understanding sit at the centre of how we work. An engineer who knows our clients' workflows can point agents at the right problem and spot when the result is subtly wrong. Without that, agents just build the wrong thing faster.

Your part is the AI development harness that makes this safe. That means sandboxed environments with synthetic data, scoped and audited access to logs and alerts, and evals and validation gates in CI. It also means firm lines, enforced by tooling, that keep production deploys and secrets in human hands, and client data out of reach of development agents.

You'll also build the agent orchestration pipelines that run in three places: in how we build software, in AI workflows inside the product our clients use, and in the internal tools our implementation team uses to onboard and configure clients.

What you'll do

Build the machine that builds the product

Most of your time goes here.

  • Build our AI development harness. Self-service infrastructure, a reproducible development environment, and the sandboxes, guardrails and evals that let agents take on more of the work safely, with results we can measure.

  • Automate quality. Build the QA automation pipeline: automated tests, validation gates and release checks that give us confidence in every change, including the ones agents write.

  • Orchestrate agents across the business. Build pipelines that run agents reliably and safely in our product workflows and our internal implementation tools, not just in engineering.

Own the platform

  • Own our infrastructure. We're migrating to ECS. You'll strengthen our ECS architecture, see the move through in safe, reversible stages, bring every resource under infrastructure as code, and retire the old deployment model.

  • Build security into the platform. Tenant-scoped credentials, per-tenant secrets, least-privilege access, and the audit trail that SOC 2 and our clients' security teams expect.

  • Make production observable. Set up the monitoring, alerting and tracing we rely on, and build playbooks for on-call and incident response which is shared amongst the team.

Work across the stack

  • Make the application changes the harness needs, such as synthetic data, test hooks and the specs agents work from.

  • Ship product. Pick up application work in TypeScript and React alongside the team. Over time, you'll learn the codebase as well as the platform it runs on.

  • Grow the team around you. Write the design notes and runbooks, pair with and review the work of other engineers, and mentor those who want to grow into infrastructure, so the platform never depends on one person.

Your first six months

  • Get the first parts of "the machine" running, and show that they make the team faster without lowering quality.

  • At the moment all of our end to end testing is done manually by our Product team. That's a massive manual overhead that bottlenecks our product development. You'll help build our AI-powered QA automation pipeline, so every change, whether a person or an agent wrote it, is tested automatically before it reaches clients.

  • Strengthen the ECS architecture and complete the move with no disruption to clients.

  • Get the platform fully into code, with tenant isolation and least privilege designed in.

  • Put in place the monitoring and on-call foundations the team will build on.

How you'll work

You'll own this area rather than work through a ticket queue. You'll decide what to build and when it's good enough, write your decisions down so others can challenge them, and tell us when something isn't worth doing. You'll work closely with Product from the start of significant work, because the platform exists to serve clients and the engineers building for them.

You and I will work together every day. We'll shape the technical direction together and think through the hard calls, and you'll have a direct line to every decision that affects your work. I'll back your judgement, and I'll expect you to push back when you think I'm wrong.

This is an individual contributor role, but we expect you to multiply the team: leading different areas at different times, and delivering through others as well as through your own work.

You'll probably enjoy this if

  • You'd rather build a platform properly than keep patching one.

  • You're product-minded. You've probably worked at a startup or scale-up, or even founded something yourself. Seeing your work out in the world, solving real problems, is what motivates you. You ask who a change is for before you ask how to build it.

  • You already work this way. Agents write much of your code, and your time goes on design, specs and judging the output. You've built AI tooling for yourself, and probably for others on your team.

  • You get satisfaction from making other engineers faster.

  • You're comfortable writing Terraform, an API endpoint and an answer to a client's security questionnaire in the same week.

  • You've been the person others come to with hard problems, and you've changed your mind publicly when the evidence said so.

This probably isn't for you if

  • You want a pure DevOps or SRE role.

  • You want to manage people right now. These opportunities might exist in the future, but for now we're small, lean and as flat as possible.

What you'll bring

Very few people match every line. If most of this describes you, we'd like to hear from you.

  • Deep, hands-on AWS. Several years running production workloads on ECS or EKS, with a solid grasp of IAM, networking and Lambda.

  • Infrastructure as code as a habit, with Terraform or CloudFormation, including bringing existing hand-built resources under code.

  • Scaling distributed systems. You've taken systems through real growth in load and data, and can teach others what you learnt.

  • Single-tenant SaaS experience. You know the isolation trade-offs and how to keep one client's data and credentials away from another's.

  • Security and compliance as part of engineering: least privilege, secrets management, and evidence for SOC 2 or ISO 27001.

  • Production experience: on-call, incidents, post-mortems, and observability tooling such as Datadog, Grafana or Honeycomb.

  • Full-stack product building. Senior TypeScript and Node.js, plus React, with a track record of shipping features end to end yourself, not just supporting the people who do.

  • Test automation and CI/CD. You've designed pipelines that test at the right levels and release safely, and you keep them fast and simple.

  • Tooling you've built for AI agents, not just used: agent configuration and orchestration, MCP servers or similar integrations, evals, automated review.

Our stack

TypeScript, Node.js, React and MongoDB Atlas, running on AWS. CircleCI and Bitbucket. AI coding agents are part of everyday work. You don't need experience of all of these.

How we hire

We want to see how you actually work, so there are no whiteboard puzzles.

  1. Screening call with me (20 minutes)

  2. Competencies interview with me (30 minutes)

  3. Technical deep dive with a few of our engineers (90 minutes)

  4. Culture fit interview with our CEO, Hemal (30 minutes)

I'll be your main point of contact throughout. You'll know what to expect before each stage, and if we don't make an offer, I'll give you feedback.

descriptionHtml:
Über IONOS

Bei IONOS verwalten wir nicht nur Server, wir prägen mit unseren Lösungen die digitale Zukunft für über 6,2 Millionen Kundinnen und Kunden weltweit. Als Europas führender Hosting-Anbieter und Pionier für unabhängige Cloud-Lösungen bauen wir eine Infrastruktur der nächsten Generation: von souveränen Cloud-Architekturen und hochperformanten GPU-Clustern bis hin zu integrierten KI-Automatisierungstools.

Was uns antreibt: Digitale Entscheidungsfreiheit für Europa und echter Impact für kleine und mittlere Unternehmen (KMU) sowie Großunternehmen. Wir arbeiten in agilen Teams, setzen auf transparente Strukturen und glauben daran, dass Exzellenz und Innovation nur mit echtem Teamgeist entstehen.

Bereit für Deinen nächsten Schritt? Werde ein Teil von IONOS und wachse mit uns.

Als Mitglied des multinationalen Security Management Teams bei IONOS SE arbeitest du für einen der größten europäischen Hoster im rasant wachsenden Cloud-Sektor und bringst dein Wissen und deine Erfahrung ein, um unsere Produkte und Systemlandschaft noch besser zu schützen. Du bist verantwortlich für das Design und den Betrieb eines integrierten Managementsystems, das unter anderem zertifizierte Bereiche nach ISO 27001, KRITIS, NIS2 umfasst und kontinuierlich ausgebaut wird. Das Ziel ist es, die Umsetzung und den Betrieb von Sicherheitsmechanismen zu fördern und zu steuern – nicht nur, um nachzuweisen, dass unsere Produkte die Sicherheitsanforderungen der Standards erfüllen, sondern auch, um den Nutzen für unsere Kund:innen und das Unternehmen zu erhöhen. Du schlägst die Brücke von ISO 27001 zu aufkommenden regulatorischen Standards wie NIS2 und KRITIS und stellst sicher, dass unsere Produkte eine grundsolide Compliance beibehalten und gleichzeitig schnelle Innovationen ermöglichen.

Aufgaben

  • Fachliche Führung & Steuerung: Führe Projektteams, Engineers und Junior Security Peers fachlich über Zertifizierungs- und Audit-Initiativen hinweg. Agiere als primäre technische Leitung für Neu- und Rezertifizierungszyklen.

  • Kontinuierliche Compliance & Audit-Durchführung: Leite die operative Planung, Durchführung und Nachbereitung interner und externer Sicherheitsaudits. Führe das Unternehmen durch den Einsatz von Echtzeit-Sicherheitsdashboards und modernen GRC-Tools hin zu einer kontinuierlichen Compliance.
  • Regulatorische & Zertifizierungsausrichtung: Gleiche unsere Zertifizierungsrahmenwerke mit sich entwickelnden regulatorischen Anforderungen ab – einschließlich der NIS2- und KRITIS-Standards.
  • Reporting & Executive Interface: Erstelle, kompiliere und präsentiere Sicherheitsmetriken und Zertifizierungsstatusberichte für das Senior Management.
  • Disziplinübergreifende Risiko- & Vendor-Unterstützung: Unterstütze Risikomanagement, Third-Party Risk Assessments (TPRM), Security Awareness und Incident Management über alle Produktlinien hinweg.

Qualifikationen

  • Hintergrund: Erfolgreich abgeschlossenes Studium der Informatik, Informationssicherheit oder vergleichbare praktische Erfahrung in Cloud-/SaaS-Hosting-Umgebungen.
  • Zertifizierungs- & Framework-Expertise: Nachweisbare Erfolge bei der erfolgreichen Leitung von ISO 27001 Audits. Praktische Vertrautheit mit DSGVO, CSA CCM und neuen Standards (NIS2/KRITIS).
  • Fähigkeit zur fachlichen Führung: Nachgewiesene Stärke darin, funktionsübergreifende Projekte zu leiten, Kolleg:innen zu mentorieren und diverse Stakeholder ohne direkte Weisungsbefugnis erfolgreich zu steuern.
  • Tooling- & Automatisierungs-Mindset: Erfahrung mit modernen GRC-Tools und automatisierter Evidenzerhebung zur Minimierung des manuellen Aufwands bei Reports.

Benefits

Hinweis zur Bewerbung

Wir wertschätzen Vielfalt und begrüßen alle Bewerbungen – unabhängig von z. B. title: Staff Product Designer
descriptionHtml:
OUR MISSION

To become the car-changing destination of choice. By combining technology, media and deep automotive expertise, we've turned how people buy, sell, advertise and lease cars on its head.

What started as a simple reviews site is now one of the largest online car-changing destinations in Europe. Last year alone we grew over 50% with nearly £3bn worth of cars bought on site, while £1.8bn of cars were listed for sale through our Sell My Car service.

In 2024 we went big and acquired Autovia - creators of AutoExpress and Evo magazines - doubling our audience overnight. Together we now have one of the biggest YouTube channels in the world with almost 10m subscribers and over 1.1 billion annual views, while we sell 1.2 million print copies of our magazines and have an annual web content reach over 350million.

And we’re a long way from done!

THE ROLE

We're looking for a Lead/Staff Product Designer to shape some of the most important experiences in our marketplace. You'll own complex, high-impact problem spaces end to end — from ambiguous discovery through to shipped, measured outcomes — and raise the bar for design craft and pace across the whole team.

This is a senior individual-contributor role with real influence. You'll partner directly with product and engineering leadership, mentor other designers, and set the standard for how design work gets done at Carwow.

A note on how we work: AI fluency is integral to the role. Our design team works AI-natively. We use Claude Code/Design (and similar tools) to move from idea to high-quality prototype in hours, not weeks, and we expect designers at this level to be genuinely fluent in this way of working, not just curious about it. If you're still designing the way teams did in 2023, this probably isn't the right role. If you've rebuilt your workflow around AI and it's made you dramatically faster and more ambitious, we'd love to talk.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own end-to-end design for a major problem space in our marketplace — buying, selling, or dealer-facing products — from discovery and framing through to launch and iteration

  • Prototype at pace using AI, getting real, testable experiences in front of users and stakeholders early and often

  • Work shoulder-to-shoulder with engineers, using AI-assisted workflows to close the gap between design intent and shipped product — ideally getting hands-on in code where it speeds things up

  • Set direction, not just execute: identify opportunities, make the case with evidence, and bring product and engineering partners with you

  • Raise the craft bar across the team through critique, mentorship, and by making your own work an example worth following

  • Champion AI-native ways of working — sharing techniques, building reusable prompts and workflows, and helping the wider team level up

  • Ground decisions in evidence, combining user research, data, and rapid experimentation

 

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • 7+ years of product design experience, with a track record of leading complex, high-impact work in consumer or marketplace products

  • Native app experience

  • A high degree of AI fluency. Hands-on, demonstrable experience using Claude Design (or an equivalent AI design/prototyping tool) as a core part of your workflow — this is critical to the role, and we'll want to see it in your portfolio and hear about it in interviews

  • Strong end-to-end craft: you can go from a fuzzy problem statement to polished, production-ready design, and everything you ship is considered

  • Comfort with ambiguity and pace — you make good decisions with incomplete information and iterate quickly

  • Excellent communication and influence: you can align senior stakeholders, tell a compelling story with your work, and hold your ground constructively

  • Experience mentoring designers and lifting the standard of a team

 

STRONGLY PREFERRED

  • Experience with Claude Code (or an equivalent AI coding agent) — enough to prototype in real code, collaborate more deeply with engineers, or ship small changes yourself

  • Marketplace, e-commerce, or two-sided platform experience

  • Familiarity with experimentation-driven product development (A/B testing, funnel analysis)

 

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

In your first six months you'll have taken ownership of a significant problem space, shipped work that measurably moves a core metric, and become someone other designers seek out — both for the quality of your craft and for how you use AI tools to work at a pace and ambition level others want to copy.

 

WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU

  • Hybrid working

  • Competitive salary to fund that dream holiday to Bali

  • Matched pension contributions for a peaceful retirement

  • Share options - when we thrive, so do you!

  • Bupa Private Healthcare, for peace of mind, plus eyecare vouchers

  • Life Assurance for (even more) peace of mind

  • Monthly coaching sessions with Spill - our mental wellbeing partner

  • Enhanced holiday package, plus Bank Holidays

    • 28 days annual leave

    • 1 day for your wedding

    • 1 day off when you move house - because moving is hard enough without work!

    • For your third year anniversary, get 30 days of annual leave per year

    • For your tenth year anniversary, get 35 days of annual leave per year

    • Option to buy 3 extra days of holiday per year

  • Work from abroad for a month

  • Inclusive parental, partner and shared parental leave, fertility treatment and pregnancy loss policies

  • Bubble childcare support and discounted nanny fees for little ones

  • The latest tech (Macbook or Surface) to power your gif-sending talents

  • Up to £500/€550 home office allowance for that massage chair you’ve been talking about

  • Generous learning and development budget to help you master your craft

  • Regular social events: tech lunches, coffee with the exec sessions, lunch 8 learns, book clubs, social events/anything else you pester us for

  • Refer a friend, get paid. Repeat for infinite money

Diversity and inclusion is an integral part of our culture. We know that diverse teams are strong teams, so we welcome those with alternative identities, backgrounds, and experiences to apply for this position. We make recruiting decisions based on experience, skills and potential, so all our applicants are treated fairly and equally.

title: Staff Product Designer
descriptionHtml:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you'll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About this role:

As a Staff Product Designer at Samsara, you will set a vision and ship work that shapes the way our customers and internal teams operate. You will partner closely with Product and Engineering leaders, set the interaction patterns and visual systems other designers build on, and build direct relationships with our most strategic customers.

This is a remote role open to candidates residing in the US.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact: helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won't be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
  • You're energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead large, ambiguous initiatives that span multiple product areas, from problem framing through launch and iteration.
  • Be a taste maker and demonstrate good judgement in your domain.
  • Regularly meet and engage with our most strategic customers to bring the customer voice alongside product data into product decisions.
  • Leverage AI tools through every step of the process, defining new ways of working and democratizing design at Samsara.
  • Stay well informed on the emerging trends, tools, and technology. Give back to the community.
  • Ship code to production across our design system, web products, and mobile apps.
  • Set the bar for what great looks like through building and shipping.

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 10+ years of product design experience designing UX/UI for web and mobile applications, with a track record of leading work that spans multiple product areas.
  • A strong portfolio and/or case studies showing design craft and quantified impact at the level of multiple product areas or platform-wide systems, not just a single feature. We cannot consider applications without a portfolio at this time.
  • Deep interaction and visual design skills, with the judgment to define new patterns other designers and teams build on.
  • AI tools in your regular design practice (e.g., Cursor, Figma Make), with shipped work you can attribute to them.
  • Experience mentoring designers formally and informally.
  • Experience partnering with senior leadership.

The compensation range shown spans approved pay zones for this role. Your primary work location determines the range applicable to you, which may be narrower than the full range displayed.

The range of annual base salary for full-time employees for this position is below. Please note that base pay offered may vary depending on factors including your city of residence, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This role is also eligible for an initial RSU grant with no vesting cliff, and ongoing refresh opportunities tied to performance, subject to plan terms and conditions. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual Base Salary$143,640—$256,500 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you're ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual's ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

title: Staff Product Engineer - AI Native
descriptionHtml:
Ready to be part of the Legal Tech revolution?

Vision:

As a leading software-as-a-service (SaaS) provider, DiliTrust is a global company dedicated to offering an integrated suite of legal and governance products. Our vision is to digitize legal departments worldwide. With an annual growth rate of over 40% since 2020, our ambition is to become the world's leading Legal Tech company, aiming for a valuation exceeding $1 billion by 2026.

Our Impact:

From generating General Meeting reports to leveraging AI-assisted contract lifecycle management, our teams in our 8 offices across France, the US, Mexico, MEA, Germany, Spain, Italy, and Canada are the driving force behind our global success. We proudly support 2,400 customers in 64 countries, with 80% of our clientele comprising listed companies in major markets such as Europe, North America, and the Middle East.

Our Recognition:

DiliTrust has been at the forefront of Legal Tech innovation, being the first Legal Tech with AI features since 2022. The company is renowned for providing a positive and entrepreneurial work environment. We are honored to have received the "Happy at Work" and "Tech at Work" labels every year since 2019.

The Role:

Lini is DiliTrust's proprietary AI engine, powering Ask Lini, Risk Detector, Document Summarization, Minute Generation, and every AI capability across the suite.

We are building a dedicated squad around it and are looking for a strong Software / Product Engineer, with a focus our platform architecture, to help us bring it to the next level.

As a Software Engineer work at the intersection of AI, product, and engineering. You will contribute to building, improving, and scaling the features that make Lini a reliable and powerful AI layer across the entire DiliTrust suite.

We are looking for an engineer who writes clean, production-ready code and is comfortable taking ownership of features end-to-end, from technical design to deployment. We also care about how you think about AI: whether you bring genuine curiosity to the product, and whether you can translate a model capability into a great user experience.

Missions

  • Write specifications as the durable asset of the project. Executable acceptance criteria, and — crucially — the non-functional requirements that specs almost never carry: data classification, endpoint × role authorization matrix, volumetry assumptions, latency and throughput budgets. These are the requirements whose later correction is superlinear, so they get decided before generation, not after.
  • Freeze the contracts before any fan-out. API schemas, types, module boundaries, invariants. Agents do not negotiate an interface in the hallway: each will make a plausible and incompatible assumption, discovered at integration.
  • Pilot coding agents with a tight brief and a bounded context — narrow tasks, defined input and output artifacts, explicit stop conditions and budgets, full traceability of what produced each change.
  • Keep producer and verifier separate. You do not sign off alone on generation you piloted, and you act as independent verifier on your peers' slices — with an adversarial brief ("find what breaks against this spec"), never "confirm this looks fine".
  • Build the asymmetric gates that make the slice safe at volume — expensive to satisfy, cheap to check: property tests, contract tests, query-count and allocation budgets, execution-plan checks, policy-as-code, backward-compatibility proofs. Written before the implementation exists, so the agent closes the feedback loop itself without consuming human attention.
  • Use code reading as a calibration instrument, not as a gate. Sample deliberately, by risk zone, to measure the real defect rate of the generator-plus-gates pair and to keep the team's mental model of its own system alive.
  • Keep work-in-progress low. Capped PR size, thin vertical slices, trunk-based with very short branches, feature flags over long-lived branches, CI as the agent's first task rather than its last. More features in flight does not mean faster delivery when the bottleneck is verification.
  • Design for blast radius. Reversibility, progressive delivery, structured logs, traces, metrics and instrumentation generated as a matter of course. On many paths, detecting in five minutes beats three days of review that prevents nothing.

Requirements

Being based in France with full working rights. Fluent in French and English.

Experience & Seniority:

  • 8+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a significant portion spent building and operating B2B SaaS platforms in production
  • Proven ownership of features across their full lifecycle — design, delivery, iteration, maintenance — on long-lived, multi-year products
  • Strong background in complex, scalable web architectures, including real modularity: you have seen where coupling stops parallel work dead

AI-Native Practice:

  • Demonstrated, sustained use of coding agents in production work — not autocomplete, but delegated implementation with review and accountability
  • A concrete, articulated view of where generated code fails: correlated defects rather than idiosyncratic ones, uniform surface quality that destroys the usual "look here" review signals, plausibility with no author to interrogate
  • Comfort being accountable for code you did not author, and the discipline to refuse a change you cannot explain

Verification & Quality:

  • Real fluency in property-based testing, contract testing, and deriving tests from the specification rather than from the code
  • Test-data strategy, including maintaining a volumetrically representative dataset as part of the verification apparatus — not a nice-to-have
  • Instinct for the difference between a rigorous check and a scalable one: does the cost of checking grow with the volume produced?

Security & Performance (non-negotiable on this role):

  • Authorization modelling in multi-tenant systems, and why declarative, centrally enforced authorization beats reviewing each endpoint. Generated code reliably checks who you are and regularly forgets whether you are allowed
  • Awareness of the attack surface specific to an agent-assisted pipeline: prompt injection through ticket descriptions, code comments and dependency READMEs; supply-chain risk on hallucinated package names; least privilege for non-human identities; and the most frequent risk of all — production data or proprietary code leaking into the development loop
  • Performance as a measured number rather than a code-reading opinion: query budgets per HTTP request, N+1, unbounded result sets, missing indexes on new query paths, network calls in loops, execution-plan review. These are invisible at test-data scale and expensive in production

Product & Team Collaboration:

  • Excellent written communication — specification writing is now a core engineering skill on this role, not documentation overhead
  • Extensive experience working directly with product managers, designers and stakeholders in a product-oriented setup
  • Strong sense of ownership and sound judgment on risk: what to build, what not to build, what residual risk is acceptable and why

Education:

  • Master's degree in Engineering or equivalent practical experience in senior SaaS environments

What this role is not

We would rather say it up front:

  • It is not a prompt-engineering role, and it is not an ML/LLM research role.
  • It is not a role where green tests are sufficient evidence. On security and performance, "the spec is met and the tests pass" is not a weak signal — it is a null one.
  • It is not a ticket queue. The profile that shrinks in an AI-native team is the one whose value was implementing assigned tickets between two boundaries.

Our Tech Stack

  • Backend: Node.js / TypeScript
  • Frontend: Vue.js 3
  • Database: PostgreSQL, MariaDB
  • DevOps: Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform
  • Cloud: GCP

Engineering apparatus you will use and help build: coding agents orchestrated deterministically in CI, aspect-scoped verification agents (authorization, performance, spec conformance, dependencies), policy-as-code, property-based and contract testing, volumetric test datasets, load and endurance gates on critical paths, feature flags, progressive delivery and end-to-end tracing.

What we offer

  • Join a fast-growing company in a friendly, international environment — engineering primarily in Paris, with further engineering presence in Berlin, Montreal and Wilmington (DE), and offices across France, Italy, Spain, Germany, Canada, the USA, Mexico and Dubai;
  • Our "Remote Policy" guarantees that you can find the right balance between "Onsite" and "Remote";
  • Last but not least, all the day-to-day benefits of the CSE, luncheon vouchers, profit sharing bonuses, etc...

Recruitment process

  • Interview with a TA team member (30/45 mins)
  • Interview with the Engineering Manager (1h)
  • Technical interview (1h30) — two parts: turning an ambiguous requirement into a specification with executable acceptance criteria, then an adversarial review of an agent-generated diff against that specification
  • Interview with the CTO (45 mins)

title: Staff Product Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Hi 👋 I’m Rich Ashworth, Director of Engineering at hyperexponential.

I lead the Model Authoring value stream that owns the products our customers use to write and manage their pricing models. An actuary might start with an Excel rater and finish with a Python model that has been reviewed, approved, and is pricing live business. Our job is to turn that into an exceptional user experience and make every step of that credible enough to trust.

I'm hiring a Staff Product Engineer to help set our technical direction and build the next version of our products. It's an individual contributor role, but influence is a huge part of it: the standards the pods work to, the shared enablers underneath the product, and the interfaces where our problems meet other teams'. You’ll be hands-on where the risk is highest.

There's no established playbook for any of this, but there’s an incredible opportunity in front of us. If this sounds like a role that would excite you, I'd love to hear from you.

About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a £7 trillion industry, which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-pound decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

About the Model Authoring team

Model Authoring owns the products our customers use to write and manage their pricing models: the model developer experience and our actuarial agent. An actuary might start with an Excel-based rater and finish with a Python model that has been reviewed, approved and is pricing live business. Our job is to make every step of that credible enough to trust. The team is distributed across our Warsaw and London offices.

As the Staff Product Engineer, you will help set the team's technical direction. This is an individual contributor role, but influence is a large part of it: you'll help define the standards the team works to, raise the technical bar across pods, and own the interfaces where our problems meet those of teams elsewhere in Technology. You'll be expected to move fast and start shaping technical conversations early. We work in an AI-native way, and you'll help define and evolve what that means here.

What you'll be doing

  • Establish a set of engineering standards across the Model Authoring pods. The standards are documented and actively referenced in code review, with new pod work conforming by default.

  • Set and own the technical direction for the team's shared enablers, including how we represent and persist models, the model registry, secure context access, and shared agentic infrastructure.

  • Establish the technical interfaces between Model Authoring and other parts of the business. Dependencies with other teams are agreed, documented, and progressing without needing to be brokered by someone else.

  • Work hands-on on the hardest problems in the stream. This is not an advisory role: we would expect you in the code where the risk is highest.

  • Help define how we work in an AI-native way. Which parts of model development and of our own engineering we hand to agents, what stays human, and what evidence we need before trusting either.

  • Visibly lift the engineers around you. You're sought out for design input across pods, and there's at least one engineer whose growth is clearly attributable to your support.

What you'll need to have done

  • Worked in an AI-native environment, and genuinely want to keep doing so. You've used AI or agentic tools in your own engineering workflow, introduced or experimented with them, and have a real view on what's worked and what hasn't.

  • Been product-focused rather than purely technical. You understand who your users are, where their pain points are, and how your technical decisions connect to commercial outcomes.

  • Set technical direction while navigating genuine ambiguity. A proven track record of owning architecture in a domain with no established playbook, and making clear calls on imperfect information rather than deferring them.

  • Owned a significant technical challenge or service end to end, with the depth to walk through it in detail - the trade-offs, the contracts, the things you'd do differently.

  • Influenced across teams. You can hold a position under challenge, genuinely listen to pushback, and persuade others - not just present your own view and hope it lands.

  • Worked effectively across distributed teams - this role spans our Warsaw and London offices, so you'll need to be comfortable building relationships and influence across both.

You're unlikely to thrive here if

  • You'd rather focus purely on the technical problem than get close to users, customer pain points, and the commercial implications of what you build.

  • You're not comfortable setting technical direction in ambiguity, or you'd rather wait for an established playbook than make a call on imperfect information.

  • You're not excited about helping define what the future of software engineering looks like and are prepared to embrace tooling and new ways of working to support this.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

Compensation

At hx, we're committed to salary transparency. You'll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we're working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we're building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don't always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that's competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Benefits

£5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.

25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).

Company pension scheme via Penfold.

Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life.

Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.

Private healthcare insurance through AXA.

Income protection and Life Insurance.

Cycle to Work Scheme.

Additional perks

Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.).

Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights.

Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry.

Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

Interview process

  1. Initial call with our Talent team

  2. Hiring Manager Interview

  3. Skills Assessment & follow-up interview

  4. Values Interview

  5. Meet the CEO

Our commitment to Diversity

hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

Next steps

If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome.

For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page.

title: Staff Product Manager, AI Agents & Assistant
descriptionHtml:
About Dashlane

Dashlane’s mission is to deliver the credential security every business and employee needs to thrive. Millions of consumers, and over 25,000 brands worldwide, such as Michelin, Air France, and Forrester, trust Dashlane for industry-leading innovations, patented zero-knowledge security, and an unmatched user experience. Founded in Paris, Dashlane has since established offices in New York and Lisbon, and has grown to more than 300 Dashlaners globally.

We're looking for people who actively use AI tools to drive efficiency, creativity, and impact in their work. At Dashlane, we drive innovation and value learning, strive for excellence in everything we do, and thrive as one team. Learn more about life at Dashlane, including how we work, how we hire, and the benefits of being a Dashlaner.

About the role

As our Staff Product Manager for Agentic Capabilities, you will own the vision, strategy and roadmap for how Dashlane becomes an interface for AI agents and assistants for consumers and businesses. Success means people hand real, valuable tasks to agents through Dashlane and keep doing it, and companies trust it enough to let their teams do the same.

You will own the product alongside senior engineers as a Staff-level individual contributor in a 0-to-1 role where standards are still unsettled. We are looking for strong familiarity with the modern AI landscape, including LLMs, assistants and agentic workflows, and sound judgment about what agents can and cannot be trusted with.

At Dashlane, we embrace a hybrid culture that combines the best of both worlds: the creativity and energy of in-person collaboration with the flexibility of remote work. Our model is designed to strengthen team connections while supporting individual productivity and work-life balance. To maximize collaboration, we come together in the office on Mondays, Tuesdays, and Thursdays, while Wednesdays and Fridays offer more flexibility for focused work.

Key Responsibilities

  • Set the direction. Form and defend a point of view on how agents and assistants should act with what Dashlane protects, for consumers and businesses, and turn it into a strategy, positioning, and multi-year plan that leadership will back.

  • Read the market and judge readiness. Keep a living view of how agent makers, assistants, browsers, identity vendors and password managers are moving. Assess how ready emerging pieces such as passkeys for agents and agent sign-in standards are, and set the triggers for acting on each.

  • Own the evidence. Run discovery on the jobs people hand to agents at home and at work. Establish who hands over real tasks and what holds them back, so your bets follow demand, not hype.

  • Connect consumer and business. Treat both as a connected problem. Turn what we learn from individuals handing tasks to agents into the visibility and controls that IT and Security teams need to govern agent access at work. Flag when a decision for one audience affects the other.

  • Own the trust commitment. Define what Dashlane promises about what an agent or model can see and do, and hold every product decision and release to that promise. Turn what agents can and cannot be trusted with into a set of durable product primitives, such as limits, approvals, records and revocation, that stay valid as agents change.

  • Shape our place in the ecosystem. Decide which agent makers and platforms we invest in and on what terms. Build the relationships and technical case that make Dashlane an easy yes for them, and for the services agents log in to. Lead Dashlane’s input to the standards that govern how agents sign in and act on someone’s behalf, so our positions reflect real customer needs and our product direction.

  • Own the numbers. Set baselines and targets for adoption, repeat use and trust, including time to a first approved agent login, how long people take to decide on an agent’s request, and how often failures are recovered without the person starting over. Be accountable for them to leadership.

  • Align the organization. Bring Design, Engineering, Security, Legal, Sales & Marketing towards one plan, establish the operating rhythm and decision framework for the team, and settle ownership where it is unclear.

In your first year:

  • By 90 days, the team's early engineering work has become a shared view of the problem, a trust model that Security and Architecture back, and proposed targets for what "working" means. You have shared a point of view on the category with Dashlane leadership.

  • By 6 months, real people are experiencing agentic value through Dashlane, engagement is recurring, and you know who gets the most value first.

  • By 12 months, people keep using it and it shows in who chooses and stays on our plans. A version for companies has a clear first slice, and you have a view on where to go next. You have a vision and roadmap for agents and assistants across B2B and B2C that leadership has backed.

Requirements

  • 8+ years in product management, including ownership of an authentication, security, identity or permissions-heavy product, and at least one product you took from zero to market with measurable success (adoption, revenue or retention) in a market that was still emerging.

  • Enough technical fluency (OAuth, passkeys, sessions, browser extensions) to follow a token-flow discussion with engineers and ask where it breaks. You don't need to write code but you must be comfortable with speaking the language of engineering.

  • Strong familiarity with the modern AI landscape, including LLMs, assistants and agentic workflows. The ability to reason about what AI can and cannot do through a product and customer lens, with working knowledge of how agents operate: tool use and standard tool interfaces, browser-driving agents, how context is kept or lost, and where they can be tricked.

  • A track record of reading a fast-moving market and turning its signals into a strategy that leadership acted on.

  • Experience running 0-to-1 discovery with small samples and incomplete information, defining success as customer outcomes rather than shipped features.

  • AI-native ways of working: you build working prototypes with AI, run discovery synthesis through it, chain agents into your own workflow, and can show concretely how it has changed how you “do product”.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English: crisp problem statements, clear 1-pagers, compelling roadmap rationale, and external narratives that shape how a category is understood.

We're Also Looking For

  • Systems thinking and platform experience. You think in systems and have shipped a platform, API, integration product or partner ecosystem that other software relies on, with outcomes you can describe: the baseline, what changed, what you cut.

  • Consumer and business experience. Experience with products that serve both individuals and businesses, and the instinct to flag early how a decision in one ripples into the other.

  • Comfort with ambiguity. You will join a team whose engineers have already started scouting ahead, and you favor action over perfection, deciding with incomplete information.

  • A collaborative spirit and low ego. As comfortable deferring to others' expertise as you are asserting your own point of view.

  • Intellectual honesty. You share results transparently, learn openly from failures, and write down the evidence that would make you move earlier, later or not at all.

  • Security standard for AI. You have a threat-model instinct (prompt injection, phishing, malicious extensions, what a compromised agent could still do) and hold AI to the same standard as security: human accountability at every consequential decision, and evaluation before anything ships.

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging at Dashlane:

As a truly international company—founded in France and distributed across France, US and Portugal—Dashlane thrives off diverse perspectives. We value all aspects of diversity: gender identity, sexual orientation, ability, ethnic origin, social background, age, lifestyle, and more. We are committed to hiring a diverse community and fostering a culture where everyone is heard and belongs. See more about this here. 

Your interview experience: 

To know what to expect once you’ve sent your application, read about how we interview and hire at Dashlane. Feel free to browse our blog to find more information about our product and how we work.

title: Staff Security Operations Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About Pleo

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

About the role

We're looking for a Staff Security Operations Engineer to join our Cybersecurity team at Pleo. In this role, you'll define and deliver the SecOps roadmap, building the detection, response, and investigation capability that protects a fast-growing fintech. If you're excited about owning a security operations function end to end, from framework-based strategy through to the code that makes it run, then this is the opportunity for you!

Who you'll be working with and reporting to

You'll report to our VP of Fraud & Security and work closely with Fraud, DevSecOps, Engineering, and Risk & Compliance. Our team is highly collaborative and dedicated to protecting Pleo's customers and their money. You'll also have the chance to partner with teams across the organisation and to bring less experienced security engineers up with you as the function matures.

What you'll be doing

As a Staff Security Operations Engineer, you will:

  • Build and own a structured SecOps roadmap grounded in well-known frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK, NIST, and CIS benchmarks.

  • Lead security investigations and digital forensics, from suspicious traffic through to full incident response, and bring the findings back into how we detect and prevent.

  • Design, tune, and scale our SIEM and logging pipeline through standardized log ingestion across services so signal isn't lost in the noise.

  • Strengthen our perimeter and authentication posture, including WAF configuration, authorisation tuning, and monitoring for suspicious traffic.

  • Protect sensitive data through DLP controls, and make sure the coverage matches where the data actually lives.

  • Improve our on-call rotation for the team, defining the alerting, escalation paths, and response SLAs that make it work.

  • Automate detection and response workflows, using code and AI to reduce manual toil and shorten time to resolution.

  • Reduce SecOps-attributed risk identified through compliance gaps, and collect the evidence that demonstrates it.

  • Build dashboards and reporting that give the team and leadership real visibility into response times, coverage, and risk reduction.

  • Work cross-functionally with engineers who don't have a security background, translating threat models into changes they can actually ship.

What you bring

You'll thrive in this role if you have:

  • 10+ years of experience in security operations, incident response, or a closely related discipline, with a proven track record of materialised risk reduction through monetary impact, incidents contained, forensics that changed outcomes.

  • A strong development and engineering background. You are comfortable writing the automation, not just specifying it.

  • Hands-on SOC and SIEM management experience, including detection engineering and log pipeline design.

  • Experience in scale-up environments, where you've built capability rather than inherited a mature one.

  • A strong understanding of cloud architectures as we use AWS. With part of our estate on GCP and how infrastructure decisions shape detection and response.

  • Demonstrated experience using AI and/or coding automation to get security controls built, implemented, and operating in practice.

  • Fintech, payments, fraud, or trust & safety experience is a real advantage, as is exposure to highly regulated environments.

  • Backgrounds that tend to do well here: incident response, IR management, SOC engineering, security engineering, DevSecOps, red or blue team.

Why is this role a good fit for you

This role is a good fit for you if:

  • You want a large blast radius. We have high-impact projects where the outcome shows up in real business metrics, at a pre-IPO company.

  • You're energised by building a function rather than maintaining one, and you'd rather set the roadmap than be handed it.

  • You enjoy raising the bar around you, growing a team of specialists and lifting the people already here.

  • You're equally at home in a threat model discussion and in an editor writing the automation that acts on it.

This role is not a good fit for you if:

  • You need a well-groomed backlog and assigned tasks in order to do your best work.

  • You'd rather stay purely strategic than get hands-on with the tooling.

  • You're not up for participating in an on-call rotation.

How you'll develop in this role

In your first 6 months at Pleo, you'll:

  • Get deep into Pleo's security landscape and our detection coverage, our logging estate, our cloud footprint to form your own view of where the biggest risks sit.

  • Publish a SecOps roadmap mapped to MITRE, NIST, and CIS, agree with Engineering, Risk & Compliance, and leadership, and start delivering against it.

  • Stand up the on-call rotation and the alert response SLAs that go with it.

  • Ship your first wave of detection and automation improvements, and establish the KPIs that show what changed.

We're committed to helping you develop your career, whether that means taking on bigger projects, stepping into leadership, or acquiring new skills. There's genuine room here for the scope of this role to grow, including into people leadership.

The location

Please note: We can hire on a remote, hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations.

Show me the benefits!

  • Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

  • Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office

  • Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis

  • We offer 25-28 days of holiday (depending on your location) + public holidays

  • For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options

  • Option to purchase 5 additional days of holiday through a salary sacrifice

  • We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far

  • Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work

The interview process

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

  1. Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.

Why Mozilla?

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people. 

The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms.

As part of the team, you will be responsible for all things related to services and infrastructure for our Enterprise products.

descriptionHtml:
Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacuna l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain.

Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.

L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

À Mines Saint-Étienne, nos centres de recherche sont le cœur battant de notre École.

Pensés comme de véritables hubs d’innovation, nos cinq Centres de Formation et de Recherche articulent leurs expertises autour de grands enjeux industriels, environnementaux, sociétaux et technologiques.

Leur mission ? Imaginer le monde de demain en alliant excellence académique et impact concret.

Vous rêvez d’une industrie propre, efficace et durable ? Le centre SPIN en fait sa priorité.

Énergie, environnement, procédés industriels… on y conçoit des systèmes pour produire mieux, avec moins.

L’objectif ? Limiter l’impact environnemental, réduire la consommation énergétique et booster l’efficacité.

🔧 Dans un monde en pleine mutation, nos équipes déploient leur créativité scientifique pour accompagner l’industrie du futur.

Et vous, prêt·e à innover à nos côtés ?

🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous

La production de béton est responsable d'environ 8 % des émissions mondiales de CO2. Ces émissions sont principalement liées à la combustion et à la décarbonatation du calcaire nécessaire à la production du ciment Portland conventionnel.

Les liants à base de magnésie (MgO) sont étudiés comme alternatives potentielles aux ciments conventionnels, avec une empreinte carbone réduite. Le magnésium nécessaire à leur production pourrait être extrait de roches non carbonatées ou de saumures riches en magnésium. Ces ressources constituent des sources alternatives de matières premières et pourraient permettre d'éviter les émissions de CO2 liées à la décarbonatation du calcaire.

Cependant, ces liants alternatifs sont encore en cours de développement et leurs mécanismes d'hydratation, leur composition et leurs propriétés mécaniques doivent être mieux compris. En particulier, la nature et la réactivité de la source de magnésium, ainsi que les conditions de formulation et de préparation, peuvent influencer la microstructure et les performances mécaniques du matériau obtenu.

L'objectif de ce stage est d'étudier différentes sources de magnésium et d'évaluer leur potentiel pour le développement de liants de type MgO-SiO2 présentant de bonnes propriétés mécaniques et un impact environnemental réduit.

Plusieurs formulations de liants seront préparées et étudiées en faisant varier la source de magnésium et différents paramètres de formulation. Les matériaux obtenus seront caractérisés à l'aide de techniques complémentaires afin d'évaluer leur composition chimique, les phases formées lors de l'hydratation, leur microstructure, leur porosité et leurs propriétés mécaniques. Les principales étapes du stage seront les suivantes :

· Étude bibliographique : synthèse des connaissances sur les liants magnésiens, leurs mécanismes d'hydratation et leurs applications potentielles.

· Caractérisation des matières premières : étude de la composition chimique et minéralogique, de la distribution granulométrique (PSD) et de la réactivité des matières premières sélectionnées.

· Formulation et préparation des liants : élaboration de pâtes de ciment de type MgO-SiO2 en utilisant différentes sources de magnésium et différents paramètres de préparation.

· Caractérisation des matériaux : analyse des pâtes hydratées par diffraction des rayons X (DRX), analyse thermogravimétrique (ATG), microscopie électronique à balayage couplée à la spectroscopie à dispersion d'énergie (MEB/EDS), mesure de la porosité accessible à l'eau et essais mécaniques.

Analyse des résultats : comparaison des différentes formulations afin d'identifier les principaux paramètres influençant leur microstructure et leurs propriétés mécaniques.

Nous accompagnons chacun de nos collaborateurs sur le chemin de l’excellence, avec la conviction qu’ensemble, nous pouvons avoir un impact durable et significatif sur notre monde.

· Un impact réel : des projets de recherche contractuelle à hauteur de 11 M€/an, majoritairement avec des partenaires industriels, un centre de culture scientifique la Rotonde qui s’engage depuis 25 ans dans la médiation des sciences avec plus de 50 000 visiteurs/an

title: Stage HSE / Veiligheid
descriptionHtml:
Hoe kun jij bijdragen?

Wil jij tijdens je stage direct bijdragen aan een veilige en gezonde werkomgeving binnen een technische productieorganisatie? Bij NX Filtration krijg je de kans om onze huidige Risico-Inventarisatie & Evaluatie (RI&E) kritisch onder de loep te nemen en te onderzoeken in hoeverre deze nog aansluit op de dagelijkse praktijk.

Onze organisatie, werkzaamheden en processen zijn continu in ontwikkeling. Dat betekent dat ook arbeidsrisico's kunnen veranderen. Tijdens deze stage voer jij daarom een onafhankelijke review uit van de bestaande RI&E en het bijbehorende Plan van Aanpak.

Je blijft daarbij niet achter je bureau zitten. Je gaat de werkvloer op, voert veiligheidsrondes uit, spreekt met medewerkers en leidinggevenden en analyseert onder andere incidenten, near misses, hazard reports, werkplekinspecties en andere beschikbare veiligheidsinformatie.

Je onderzoekt verschillende werkomgevingen binnen NX Filtration, waaronder productie, logistiek, maintenance & facilities, laboratorium/QC en kantoor.

De centrale vraag tijdens jouw stage is:

“In hoeverre sluit de huidige RI&E van NX Filtration aan op de actuele risico's binnen de organisatie en welke verbetermaatregelen hebben de hoogste prioriteit?”

Wie zijn wij

NX Filtration produceert membraanfilters die wereldwijd worden gebruikt om de kleinste vervuilingen uit water te filteren. Denk hierbij aan vervuilingen zoals nanoplastics, organische stoffen, kleurstoffen, medicijnresten, bacteriën en virussen. Dit heeft geresulteerd in nieuwe en eenvoudige processen voor de behandeling van water, het hergebruik van afvalwater en de productie van drinkwater. Het motto van NX Filtration is “schoon en betaalbaar water voor iedereen”. In 2024 is een geheel nieuwe, zeer moderne fabriek in Hengelo in gebruik genomen.


Wat vragen we van jou?

  • Je volgt een relevante HBO-opleiding, bijvoorbeeld: Integrale Veiligheidskunde, Milieukunde, Technische Bedrijfskunde, of een vergelijkbare technische of veiligheidskundige opleiding.

  • Je hebt interesse in HSE, arbeidsveiligheid, productieprocessen en continu verbeteren.

  • Je werkt analytisch, zorgvuldig en gestructureerd.

  • Je durft medewerkers en leidinggevenden op verschillende niveaus te interviewen.

  • Je kunt waarnemingen objectief vastleggen en vertalen naar concrete en uitvoerbare verbetervoorstellen.

  • Je bent praktisch ingesteld en vindt het leuk om zowel zelfstandig als met verschillende afdelingen samen te werken.

  • Je beheerst de Nederlandse taal goed en bij voorkeur ook de Engelse taal.

Wat bieden we jou?

Een impactvolle stage op het gebied van HSE en arbeidsveiligheid, met een stagevergoeding á €500,00 (o.b.v. 40 uur). En omdat gezond werken ook belangrijk is, staat elke maandag en woensdag vers fruit voor je klaar.

title: Stage of Afstuderen: Optimalisatie van Machine-inspecties
descriptionHtml:
Wat ga je doen?

Binnen Customer Service voert Voortman periodieke machine-inspecties uit om de technische staat van machines te beoordelen en klanten te adviseren over onderhoud, reparaties en mogelijke verbeteringen. Deze inspecties vormen een belangrijke basis voor het verhogen van de betrouwbaarheid, prestaties en levensduur van machines.

Het huidige inspectieproces is door de jaren heen organisch gegroeid. Hierdoor worden inspectievragen niet altijd op dezelfde manier geïnterpreteerd, verschillen beoordelingen tussen monteurs en worden bevindingen niet overal uniform vastgelegd. Ook de rapportage richting klanten kan op onderdelen duidelijker, consistenter en meer actiegericht worden ingericht.

Tijdens deze opdracht analyseer je het volledige machine-inspectieproces en ontwikkel je een vernieuwde werkwijze die aansluit bij de huidige en toekomstige behoeften van onze serviceorganisatie. Daarbij kijk je niet alleen naar de inhoud van inspectievragen, maar ook naar de manier waarop inspecteurs informatie verzamelen, beoordelingen uitvoeren, bevindingen vastleggen en resultaten communiceren naar klanten.

Je houdt je onder andere bezig met:

  • Het analyseren van het huidige machine-inspectieproces en het identificeren van verbeterpunten;

  • Het ontwikkelen van een logische en uniforme structuur voor machine-inspecties;

  • Het herformuleren en standaardiseren van bestaande inspectievragen;

  • Het opstellen van duidelijke beoordelingscriteria voor de technische staat van machineonderdelen;

  • Het ontwikkelen van een uniforme methode voor het vastleggen van metingen, bevindingen, foto's en aanbevolen acties;

  • Het verbeteren van inspectierapportages zodat technische bevindingen overzichtelijk, eenduidig en actiegericht worden gepresenteerd;

  • Het opstellen van een implementatievoorstel voor het vernieuwde inspectieproces binnen Customer Service.

Het eindresultaat is een praktisch en onderbouwd verbeterplan waarmee Voortman machine-inspecties wereldwijd op een uniforme manier kan uitvoeren en klanten nog beter kan ondersteunen met duidelijke inspectierapportages en onderhoudsadviezen.


Wij vragen

  • HBO studie in de richting van Technische bedrijfskunde, Werktuigbouwkunde, Mechatronica of vergelijkbaar.

Wij bieden

  • Een vergoeding: €600,- per maand;

  • Reiskostenvergoeding: zodat jij geen onnodige kosten maakt;

  • Apparatuur en materialen: bijvoorbeeld een laptop, speciaal gereedschap of software;

  • Ervaren coach: goede begeleiding is belangrijk en dus krijg je een vaste coach om je te ondersteunen;

  • Ruimte voor persoonlijke ontwikkeling.

Over Voortman

Wat in 1968 begon in een kippenschuur in Rijssen, is uitgegroeid tot wereldspeler in CNC-staalbewerkingsmachines. Met een team van meer dan 750 collega’s wereldwijd ontwikkelen en bouwen we niet alleen high-end machines, maar ook slimme software en service waarop klanten kunnen vertrouwen. Deze 3 krachtige bouwstenen maken ons Twentse, internationale familiebedrijf uniek.

title: Stagiaire Chargé(e) du développement et du mécénat
descriptionHtml:
Vous souhaitez rejoindre une équipe engagée et bienveillante, prendre part à un projet innovant d’intérêt général qui rassemble l’Etat, les entreprises et l’ensemble des membres de l'écosystème de la RSE sur tout le territoire, acquérir de solides compétences en levée de fonds ainsi qu’un réseau professionnel riche ?

Rejoignez-nous, nous recherchons actuellement notre stagiaire chargé(e) du développement et du mécénat.

Description de la Communauté “Les entreprises s’engagent”

“Les entreprises s’engagent”, c’est la Communauté des entreprises françaises engagées, portée par le Ministère du travail et de l’emploi, France Travail et l’association “Les entreprises s’engagent” qui réunit les mécènes de la Communauté.

Première initiative publique-privée du genre, nous animons des coalitions inédites qui réunissent, dans chaque département français, les entreprises de toutes tailles, mais aussi les services de l'État et les collectivités, des décideurs, des associations et des leaders engagés issus de toutes sphères.

Notre Communauté rassemble à ce jour plus de 100 000 entreprises, 101 clubs départementaux et plus de 500 personnes mobilisées pour faire vivre le mouvement quotidiennement partout en France - avec pour ambition d’atteindre 150 000 entreprises d’ici 2027.

Notre conviction est que l'entreprise, quelle que soit sa taille, a un rôle clé à jouer pour répondre aux grands défis sociaux, sociétaux et environnementaux de notre époque.

Nos missions :

  • Nous donnons aux entreprises les moyens d’agir, via la mise à disposition d’outils et de dispositifs d’engagement clé en main et l’organisation d’événements de sensibilisation et de passage à l’action.

  • Nous fédérons et favorisons le dialogue entre dirigeants d’entreprises engagées partout en France, grâce au 101 clubs départementaux.

  • Nous portons la voix des entreprises engagées, valorisons leurs bonnes pratiques et imaginons collectivement l’entreprise de demain.

Description du pôle développement

Votre stage se déroulera entièrement au sein de l’équipe nationale, en contribuant au pôle chargé du développement de la Communauté et de l'Association des mécènes composé d’une directrice, d’une responsable développement, d’une chargée de développement et d’une responsable marketing.

Le pôle développement a pour mission :

  • d’accompagner, d’outiller et de suivre l’activité des grandes entreprises de la Communauté Les entreprises s’engagent et des réseaux d’entreprises partenaires ;

  • de collecter des fonds auprès d’entreprises mécènes de la Communauté via différentes structures, programmes ou territoires à soutenir ;

  • de redistribuer ces fonds à des projets et structures d’intérêt général via des appels à projets ;

  • d’animer les cercles de mécènes et réseaux de partenaires privés.

Le pôle développement fait le lien avec l’ensemble des autres pôles, afin de synthétiser les programmes et ressources à présenter aux entreprises mécènes.

Missions liées au développement financier de la Communauté auprès des entreprises (mécénat/partenariats) :

  • Participer à la relation grands comptes et aux actions de prospection (rendez-vous de prospection entreprises, rédactions de notes, préparations de supports, événements de prospection) ;

  • Participer à la fidélisation des mécènes et l’animation des Cercles de mécènes (organisation de rdvs, réalisation de présentations, rédaction de notes, rédaction d’une newsletter mensuelle, organisations d’évènements et suivi des relations) ;

  • Suivre les tâches sur les outils de l’équipe (Salesforce, Notion, Drive etc.) ;

  • Veille sur la RSE et la philanthropie des entreprises françaises.

Profil recherché

Vous êtes actuellement en recherche de stage de césure ou de fin d’études et vous souhaitez développer vos compétences en matière de mécénat et de responsabilité sociale des entreprises, mieux connaître les politiques publiques en matière d’emploi, d’insertion professionnelle et de développement durable et allier des missions liées à la recherche de fonds, la communication, les relations publiques et l’événementiel. Vous avez une sensibilité concernant les enjeux d’inclusion et de transition écologique.

Compétences :

  • Rigueur organisationnelle ;

  • Qualité de présentation écrite et orale ;

  • Polyvalence et prise d’initiative pour travailler en équipe dans une dynamique d’amélioration continue, et passer à l’action avec un objectif de résultat ;
